CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to assess the ongoing management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, along with a review of recent symptom patterns and treatment efficacy.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a mixed response to the current treatment regimen. He states that while his anxiety levels have shown some improvement, he continues to experience significant fluctuations in mood and increased episodes of tension-type headaches, now occurring three times per week. The intensity of these headaches has escalated, with ratings reaching up to 5 out of 10, particularly during stressful work periods. He reports that ibuprofen remains effective but is concerned about the increasing frequency of use.
Sleep quality has not improved; Mr. Smith is still averaging around 5 to 6 hours of sleep per night, with persistent nocturnal awakenings. He notes that trazodone has been less effective, and he has been using gabapentin more frequently to aid sleep, which has resulted in grogginess upon waking. He expresses frustration with this cycle, stating that the mindfulness techniques are becoming less effective as his stress levels rise.
Persistent fatigue continues to be a significant concern, especially in the mornings, with Mr. Smith reporting that he feels increasingly lethargic throughout the day. He denies any new symptoms such as chest pain or significant weight changes, but he notes a slight increase in irritability.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 250 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime (consider dose adjustment) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime (continued) 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 7. Topiramate 100 mg daily (continued) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (consider increased frequency) 9. Gabapentin 100 mg at bedtime (increased frequency noted)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, where project demands are contributing to his elevated stress levels. He has been attempting to incorporate more physical activity into his routine but reports that fatigue has limited his motivation. His dietary habits remain consistent, with an emphasis on whole foods, and he continues to abstain from alcohol while limiting caffeine intake.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Persistent anxiety levels; sleep disruptions reported; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms. - Neurological: Increased headache frequency and intensity; no dizziness or visual disturbances reported. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue noted, particularly in the mornings, with no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented, appears fatigued; mood appears anxious but cooperative. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; tenderness noted in the bilateral temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears anxious with moderate distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 250 mg daily. Due to the persistent anxiety symptoms, consider increasing the dosage to 300 mg daily after discussing potential side effects with Mr. Smith. 2. Insomnia: Trazodone efficacy appears diminished; consider increasing the dose to 75 mg at bedtime. Gabapentin may be adjusted to 200 mg at bedtime to address sleep issues while monitoring for adverse effects. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Advise Mr. Smith to maintain a headache diary to track frequency and triggers. Consider a preventive strategy with an increase in topiramate dosage to 150 mg daily if headaches continue to escalate. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage Mr. Smith to keep a sleep diary and consider cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for insomnia and anxiety management. Discuss potential lifestyle modifications, including a structured sleep schedule and relaxation techniques.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-10-01 to monitor symptom changes, evaluate the efficacy of medication adjustments, and address any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to implement additional stress management strategies and to maintain open communication regarding his treatment response.
